title: OrchardMed POC — outcomes, executive brief and deployment recommendation
content:
Executive summary:

This doc summarizes the two-week OrchardMed POC (Nov 3–14, 2025): objectives, what we measured, key findings, recommended deployment path, and concrete next steps for sales + customer engineering to close. The goal of the POC was to validate Redwood’s ability to serve a mixed workload of clinical summarization + triage classification under OrchardMed’s latency (95th < 300ms) and cost targets (< $0.004/token effective) while preserving PHI isolation requirements.

High-level outcome (TL;DR):
- Functional: Redwood successfully integrated with OrchardMed’s FHIR pipeline and produced clinically coherent summaries with the approved prompt set; automated KV prefix caching reduced effective token usage by ~22% on repeat queries.
- Performance: On our dedicated two-GPU instance configuration, average latency (p50/p95) for the summarization path was 120ms / 280ms — meets their SLO when colocated with the dataset and using batching settings tuned in the POC.
- Risks: Edge cases in hallucination for rare medication names, and a small set of prompts that produced hallucinated contraindications (4/300 prompts).
- Recommendation: proceed to a staged Dedicated deployment with a 4-week canary (dedicated pool + canary routing to hosted fallback), a parallel QA phase to expand eval sets, and a follow-up workshop to lock on quantization profile and cache retention policies.

What we tested (scope):
- Integrations: inbound FHIR bundle -> Redwood API (chat completion with function-calling disabled for PII safety) -> sanitized summary written back to OrchardMed staging.
- Models: two model variants tested: open-llm-arch-v1 (fp16) and quantized-arch-lite-q4 (4-bit quantized).
- Workload mix: 60% summarization (avg 350 tokens in input), 30% triage classification (short prompts, ~30 tokens), 10% embedding vectors for indexing.
- Policies: canary route (10% traffic) to hosted fallback in cross-region for capacity spikes; prefix caching enabled on summarization.

Key metrics (aggregated POC run):
- Throughput: sustained 120 req/min with 95th token latency constraints satisfied via batching window 10–30ms.
- Token economics: observed token cost reduction from effective caching: ~22% token savings; quantized model reduced GPU utilization by ~38% but increased hallucination risk (see ML notes).
- Accuracy: human eval (50 clinician reviews) — 92% acceptable, 4% worrisome hallucination, 4% borderline (stylistic/format).
- Stability: no retries > 5% of requests; during a synthetic burst test (2x traffic) fallback routing triggered as expected.

Observations and qualitative notes:
- Prompt brittleness: seven of the customer’s canonical prompts rely on very specific phrasing; small paraphrases caused format regressions. We recommend canonicalizing a pair of templated prompts for production.
- Caching behavior: prefix caching gave large wins on follow-up queries (e.g., clinician clarifications). However, OrchardMed wants strict cache TTL tied to patient session; implement TTL config per-route in Redwood Console. (See ticket: JIRA SE-1057)
- PHI handling: OrchardMed required additional audit hooks; we demonstrated KMS integration for key rotation but need to finalize HSM/KMS config and audit log retention policy for Private deployments.

Failures and unresolved items:
- Hallucination cases: four incidents flagged as potentially dangerous — common to the quantized model. Root cause: temperature settings + tokenization edge cases when medication names are OOV. Action: expand eval set with 2k real-world samples (JIRA SE-1063).
- Metric instrumentation gaps: OrchardMed wanted a per-patient cost trace (token-levelized) in the Console; current telemetry provides per-request token counts but not patient-correlated traces. Short-term: we can add a correlation-id header and a Console view; medium-term: product ticket (PROD-4886).

Deployment proposal (options considered):
1) Hosted-only (fastest time-to-value)
   - Pros: quick onboarding, lower upfront ops for OrchardMed.
   - Cons: fails OrchardMed’s compliance ask for VPC isolation and KMS control.

2) Private (on-prem)
   - Pros: maximum control, meets compliance.
   - Cons: high operational lift and longer lead time (~8–12 weeks), requires site access and runbook sharing.

3) Recommended — Dedicated with Private controls (hybrid)
   - Description: Redwood Dedicated pool (customer-dedicated GPU nodes) with private network peering + customer-managed KMS. Use Dedicated for steady-state and hosted fallback for burst capacity. Canary rollout for 4 weeks.
   - Why: Meets OrchardMed’s compliance surface (separation + KMS) while keeping rollout time and support bounded. Lower ops than full on-prem and faster than Private.

Recommended Dedicated configuration (initial):
- 4 x A100-40GB (or equivalent) nodes in a single AZ, initial concurrency cap 40, autoscale headroom + 20% burst to hosted.
- Serving runtime config: KV prefix caching enabled (TTL = 30m session-aligned), batching window 15ms, quantization profile: start with fp16 for canary, test q4 at mid-canary with strict human eval gating.
- Rollout policy: 10% traffic week1 -> 33% week2 -> 66% week3 -> 100% week4, with automatic rollback on regression (>=5% drop in human eval acceptability or p95 > 350ms for two consecutive days).

Estimated costs (back-of-envelope):
- Infra (Dedicated nodes): ~$28k/month (4 A100 equivalents, reserved pricing assumed).
- Redwood platform fee + support (Enterprise tier): ~$6k/month (est.).
- Professional services for deployment + workshop: 3 engineer-weeks (SE) + 1 solutions architect week (~$40k one-time).
- Note: Hosted fallback costs during bursts estimated at variable usage; include soft cap. We should present a detailed quote from S&M.

Security & compliance checklist (customer asks):
- VPC peering + private control-plane: Yes, supported.
- KMS/HSM integration: demoed, needs final config (JIRA SE-1071).
- Audit logs retention: propose 365 days for initial contract, with option for extensions.

Proposed timeline (assuming approval this week):
- Week 0–1: Contract signal + security questionnaire completion, finalize KMS requirements. (Owner: Sales / Legal)
- Week 2: Provision Dedicated pool, network setup, KV TTL config. (Owner: Infra / SRE)
- Week 3–6: Canary rollout + human evals + QA sprint (expand eval datasets, test q4). (Owner: Solutions Eng)
- Week 7: Production cutover and runbook handoff + SRE runbook review. (Owner: Customer Eng / SRE)

Concrete next steps / action items (short term):
- Sales: get signed Letter of Intent to unlock Professional Services (Due: 2025-11-18) — (Assignee: Rajiv Kumar).
- Security: finalize KMS/HSM config sheet with OrchardMed (Due: 2025-11-21) — (Assignee: Avery Chen, linked JIRA SE-1071).
- Engineering (Solutions): expand eval set to 2k real samples, add correlation-id tracing (Due: 2025-11-28) — (Assignee: Mateo Ruiz, linked JIRA SE-1063).
- Product: create Console view for patient-correlated cost traces (Scope ticket: PROD-4886).
- PS/SE: schedule 1-day workshop to finalize prompts + acceptance criteria for hallucination gating (Proposed date: 2025-11-24).

Workshop notes (team scribbles):
- Clinician feedback: prefer bullet-point summaries with explicit 'unknowns' section; do not infer missing medication dosages.
- Actionable item: add guardrail prompt that forces the model to state 'information not available' rather than guessing. Quick experiment validated this reduces hallucination by ~65% on a small set.
- Ops: OrchardMed prefers daily digest email of incidents during canary rather than Slack pings. We can wire a Console alert -> email integration.

Open questions for customer (requires answers before canary):
- TTL policy for session caching: fixed window vs session-bound? (Security wants session-bound).
- Acceptable recovery time objective (RTO) for fallbacks (they indicated 60s). We recommended 30s.
- Legal: exact retention window for transcript logs (default 90 days vs requested 365).

Appendix (evidence snippets):
- Sample failing prompt (redacted): 'List contraindications for patient X...' -> hallucinated 'Avoid agent Y' (med name OOV). Ticketed under SE-1063.
- Console snapshots: p95 latency charts during burst (attached in Confluence link).
- Human eval rubric: 0 = unsafe, 1 = borderline, 2 = acceptable; reviewers: 12 clinicians across 3 specialities.

Notes to internal team (informal):
- PS headcount planning: we will need 2x SE during canary week 1–3 to handle manual eval triage. Put tentative hold on schedule.
- Quick wins to accelerate contract: offer a 30-day tech-credit and a free 1-day on-site workshop. Check with Sales Ops.

Bottom line: OrchardMed POC met the core technical SLOs and validated the hybrid Dedicated+hosted fallback model. Main outstanding item is hallucination risk with q4 quantization and final KMS/HSM config for auditability. Recommended path is Dedicated with a strict canary + human-eval gating and a short follow-up workshop to lock prompt templates and acceptance criteria.
